The seed satisfies the stated inequalities, the Hall obstruction is exact, and the general splice and objective calculations work. However, §3 gives an incorrect periodic retained-selection pattern. Taken literally, that pattern violates the whole-board inequalities and contradicts the claimed collar agreement.The required correction is
$$\boxed{
(0,0),(0,1),(0,5),(1,2),(1,4)
\quad\longrightarrow\quad
(0,1),(0,3),(0,5),(1,2),(1,4).
}$$
With this single correction, I accept the intended construction and its fractional-relaxation conclusion. The correction does not change the free-variable table, matching-edge weights, finite seed, or objective formulas: the actual finite-board retained set defined in §1.1 already has the correct phases.The checks below are exact substitutions into the supplied rational data and a written all-length argument. $$5+6i,\qquad 7+6i\qquad(0\le i\le m).$$
The additional row-zero sites are
$$3+6i\qquad(0\le i\le m+1),$$
together with column  $1$ . None of the withdrawals affects row zero. Consequently,
$$R\cap\{r=0\}
=
\{(0,1),(0,3),\ldots,(0,6m+9)\}.$$
Thus the interior retained phases on row zero are precisely  $1,3,5$ .The displayed §3 pattern instead retains phases  $0,1,5$ . At an interior top-row vertex of phase  $0$ , such as  $(0,24)$ , that erroneous periodic assignment has: $t_{(0,24)}=1$ ;both horizontal neighbors retained, hence occupations  $1,1$ ;the lower neighbor  $(1,24)$  an old endpoint, hence occupation  $1$ .It therefore violates a whole-board wedge:
$$t_{(0,24)}+o_{(0,23)}+o_{(0,25)}
=3>2.$$
It also violates the full selected-degree inequality. The vertex has grid degree  $3$ , so its left side is
$$(3-1)\cdot1+(1+1+1)=5>3.$$
There is also a literal collar mismatch: $(0,24)$  is a forced blank under §1.1, but retained in the stated periodic pattern. $(0,21)$  is retained under §1.1, but absent from the stated periodic retained phases.Replacing  $(0,0)$  by  $(0,3)$  removes both problems. The rest of this audit uses the retained set actually prescribed by §1.1, equivalently that corrected periodic pattern.2. The complete domain and terminal Hall set now checkWrite  $a=6m$ . The whole-board inequalities follow from these checks and the actual domainThe new definitions permit a short general verification of the whole-board strengthening.For a free vertex  $v$ , let  $z_v$  be its number of forced-blank neighbors. Since no free vertex is adjacent to  $R$ ,

The reduced degree inequality is

The whole-board wedges at free vertices follow by cases:Two free neighbors: the reduced wedge.One old and one free neighbor: the anchor inequality.Two old neighbors:  $b_v\ge2$ , hence  $t_v=0$ .A forced-blank neighbor: the remaining bound follows from the capacities.At an old endpoint or forced blank,  $t_v=0$ , so its wedge and degree inequalities follow from  $0\le o_u\le1$ .Finally, under the actual §1.1 domain, every retained vertex has no retained or free neighbor and has at most one old-endpoint neighbor.
